INTRODUCING AMIRA

Guided by educators.
Discovered by learners.

One classroom can have many starting points. Repeated questions stretch a teacher’s attention, while some students need another hint to move forward. AMIRA is designed around that moment: a learner’s next step, guided by their teacher.

Teachers shape the guidance

Set the instructions, teaching approach, and materials that reflect your learning goals.

Students work through the next step

Ask questions, test a hint, and explain what they have understood.

See the learning flow

How should AMIRA help?

Be a patient web development mentor.

  • Start with what the student has already tried.
  • Offer small hints the student can test.
  • Ask the student to explain why the fix worked.

FROM A SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT CLASSROOM

Learning to code, one small experiment at a time.

The challengeLearners arrived with different levels of experience. Recurring technical questions divided the teacher’s attention.

The approachStudents tried AMIRA’s hints, noted where AI helped, and discussed the reasoning behind their changes with the teacher.

The classroom practiceThe 2025 manuscript documents gradual guidance, reflection, and coaching as part of the learning process.

Web/Android chat, a system-prompt editor, subject management, and PDF resources. Prompt Preset and Learning Log are described in the classroom manuscript.

A FEW THINGS TO KNOW

A little more
about AMIRA.

Who is AMIRA for?

AMIRA’s initial focus is teachers and students in secondary and vocational education. Its early classroom practice began in web programming lessons at an Indonesian vocational school. Broader learning contexts remain part of the product direction.

What does the teacher control?

Teacher-defined instructions and materials shape how AMIRA supports a learner. Educators continue to guide reflection, check understanding, and make teaching and assessment decisions.

Can I try a live demo?

AMIRA’s earlier app was used in classroom practice, and the platform is now being rebuilt. This website provides prepared interactive examples. Public access to the new app will be announced when it is ready; contact us to discuss the rebuild or a potential school pilot.

Can AI responses be wrong?

Yes. Students should test suggestions and compare them with their learning materials. Teachers remain involved in reviewing understanding and decisions.
